chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The blood-money (diyah) is inherited by the heirs according to the shares of inheritance, except for the maternal brothers, for they do not inherit anything from the blood-money.

key_terms.الْإِخْوَةَ مِنَ الْأُمِّ: Maternal brothers (siblings sharing only the mother)

ai.seo_question: Do maternal brothers inherit blood money (diyah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that blood-money (diyah) is treated as a distinct estate distributed according to standard inheritance shares, yet it introduces a specific exception where maternal brothers are excluded. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between general inheritance rights and the specific eligibility for diyah, reflecting the nuanced application of Quranic principles to financial compensation. The exclusion underscores the unique status of maternal kin in this context, differing from their inclusion in other forms of estate distribution.
